items.title: getSubGroups filter change removes the canView-global bypass, but V2 canView(group) may not cover hierarchy semantics
items.body: In GroupResource.getSubGroups (line 176-180), the filter was changed from `g -> canViewGlobal || auth.groups().canView(g)` (where canViewGlobal = auth.groups().canView()) to simply `auth.groups()::canView`. In V1, GroupPermissions.canView(group) returns true if canView() (global) OR canManage() OR per-group permission, so the behavior is equivalent. In V2, GroupPermissionsV2.canView(group) returns true if the admin has MANAGE_USERS/VIEW_USERS roles OR hasPermission(group.getId(), VIEW, MANAGE). The subtle issue: in V2, an admin with a fine-grained 'view' permission on a parent group but not on child groups will not see the child groups in the children listing, whereas the previous code with canViewGlobal would show all children if the admin had global view. This is arguably correct for fine-grained permissions (per-group scoping), but it means the 'view' permission is no longer inherited down the group hierarchy — an admin with view on a parent group cannot see its subgroups unless they also have view on each subgroup or on all-groups. This is a significant semantic change for the subgroups listing endpoint that should be verified as intended; if hierarchy inheritance is expected, canView should walk up the parent chain like UserPermissions.evaluateHierarchy does for users.

items.title: Group removal calls V2-unsupported permission teardown
items.body: registerListener still handles GroupModel.GroupRemovedEvent by calling management(...).groups().setPermissionsEnabled(group, false) whenever ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ is enabled. This PR makes management() return MgmtPermissionsV2 when ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2 is enabled, and GroupPermissionsV2.setPermissionsEnabled throws UnsupportedOperationException. If both features are on, deleting a group fails the admin event listener and can abort the removal. The listener must no-op (or use a V2 cleanup) when the V2 evaluator is active.

items.title: Scope name constants duplicated between GroupPermissions and AdminPermissionsSchema
items.body: GroupPermissions defines MANAGE_MEMBERSHIP_SCOPE = 'manage-membership', MANAGE_MEMBERS_SCOPE = 'manage-members', VIEW_MEMBERS_SCOPE = 'view-members' (lines 50-52), which are identical to AdminPermissionsSchema.MANAGE_MEMBERSHIP, MANAGE_MEMBERS, VIEW_MEMBERS. The duplication risks drift if scope names change. The class should reference AdminPermissionsSchema constants instead of redefining them. This is a maintainability issue, not a functional bug.

items.title: Java MessageFormat syntax in an i18next-rendered bundle breaks interpolation
items.body:
The account UI (keycloak.v3) renders these messages with i18next, which interpolates `{{0}}`-style placeholders. Every other error message in this file still uses `{{0}}`.

The new value `Attribute {0} must have at least {1} and at most {2} {2,choice,0#values|1#value|1<values}.` uses Java MessageFormat placeholders and a `choice` format. i18next does not understand either. Users will see the literal text `{0}`, `{1}`, `{2}` and `{2,choice,0#values|1#value|1<values}` instead of the attribute name and limits.

The change appears to have been made only to satisfy the new HTML verifier, since the `<` inside the choice is whitelisted for this key. It should be reverted to the `{{0}}` form, or use i18next pluralization.

items.title: owasp-java-html-sanitizer 20240325.1 is used without a stated policy for URL schemes on allowed elements; combined with the anchor-stripping logic this leaves anchor validation entirely to string comparison
items.body: The PR adds `com.googlecode.owasp-java-html-sanitizer:owasp-java-html-sanitizer:20240325.1` to verify message HTML. The `POLICY_SOME_HTML` policy allows `br`, `p`, `strong`, `b` with no attributes and no URL policy, and `POLICY_NO_HTML` allows nothing. Because `santizeAnchors` removes all `<a>` tags from the value before sanitization (see the anchor finding), the sanitizer never gets the chance to validate `href` values (e.g. reject `javascript:` URLs) in translations. The version 20240325.1 is recent enough, but the design means the sanitizer dependency is effectively only used to strip non-whitelisted tags, and all anchor safety relies on exact string equality with the English source. If a translation's anchor matches the English anchor textually, its `href` is never checked by the sanitizer. The policy should allow `a` with `href` restricted to safe schemes (e.g. `allowAttributes("href").matching(uris().withSchemes("http","https","mailto"))`) and the anchor comparison should happen after sanitization.

items.title: `missing_backup_codes` message points to a regeneration feature that does not exist
items.body:
Users who enabled 2FA before this migration have `backupCodes = null` and get "No backup codes found. Please generate them in your settings."

There is no UI to generate or regenerate backup codes. The only path is to disable 2FA (which needs a working TOTP code) and enable it again. The message should describe that path, or a regeneration feature should be added.

items.title: Missing-backup-codes message points at a settings action that does not exist
items.body: missing_backup_codes tells the user to generate codes in settings. This PR only creates codes during 2FA setup and clears them on disable; there is no regenerate control. Users who enabled 2FA before the migration have backupCodes null and will see this error on Lost access, with no way to follow the instruction except fully disabling and re-enabling 2FA. The string should describe that actual path.

items.title: saveChanges does nothing useful
items.body: `saveChanges` calls `update({})`, and the server `update` action does nothing but re-render. It is also not referenced from the template.

items.title: Template hides the entire hosts table (and shows nothing) when there are zero hosts, with no empty-state message
items.body: `{{#if embedding.embeddable_hosts}}` wraps the whole table. When no hosts exist, the admin sees only the 'Add Host' button with no explanation, and — combined with the EmbeddingSerializer `embed: :ids` issue — `embedding.embeddable_hosts` may be undefined or an array of undefined entries even when hosts exist, causing the table to render with broken rows or not at all. Add an `{{else}}` branch with an empty-state message (e.g. i18n 'admin.embedding.no_hosts'), and ensure the serializer actually embeds host objects so the `if` evaluates correctly.

items.title: Remote article retrieval can follow redirects to internal services
items.body: The embed URL's hostname is checked against the configured host before retrieval, but `open(url)` follows HTTP redirects without revalidating the destination. A URL on the allowed host that redirects to an internal address can therefore make the application server fetch internal resources; the URL's port is also unrestricted. Validate every redirect destination and restrict schemes, ports, and private-network addresses before fetching.

items.title: Host comparison is case-sensitive and the same-level subdomain branch is wrong
items.body: `URI(...).host` is not normalised, so `Example.com` will not match the instance hostname. The sibling-subdomain branch compares everything after the first label for hosts with the same number of labels. For `foo.co.uk` against `bar.co.uk`, or an unrelated site such as `a.example.com` against `b.example.com`, it treats them as the same domain. Beyond that, `URI(...).path` is empty for `http://example.com`, and a trailing slash is kept, so the displayed name can end in `/`. The same URI is also re-parsed several times.

items.title: Changing the site default locale leaves cached fallback results stale
items.body: The fallback chain depends on the runtime `SiteSetting.default_locale`, but the translation cache is keyed only by translation key, active locale, and backend. If the site default locale changes, cached translations for keys missing in the active locale continue returning the old fallback translation until the cache is evicted or cleared, even though lookups should now use the new default.

cal.com__10600.text: The exported function TwoFactor handles backup codes and is in BackupCode.tsx. Inconsistent naming.
Error message mentions 'backup code login' but this is a disable endpoint, not login

Backup code validation is case-sensitive due to the use of indexOf(). This causes validation to fail if a user enters uppercase hex characters, as backup codes should be case-insensitive for a better user experience.

Because backupCodes are decrypted and mutated in memory before being written back, two concurrent login requests using the same backupCode could both pass this check and update, so a single backup code may effectively be accepted more than once if used concurrently, weakening the intended one-time-use semantics.

Object URL for backup codes is not revoked on component unmount, leading to a potential memory leak. This can cause increased memory usage over time, especially if the component is mounted and unmounted frequently.

discourse-graphite__10.text: The EmbeddableHost model's before_validation callback calls self.host.sub! to strip http://, https://, and path segments, but if self.host is nil, this raises NoMethodError.

The update and destroy methods in Admin::EmbeddableHostsController do not validate the existence of the EmbeddableHost record retrieved by ID. If EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first returns nil (i.e., the host does not exist), attempting to call methods on the nil object (e.g., save_host or destroy) will result in a NoMethodError.
record_for_host compares lower(host) = ? but does not normalize the parameter’s case, so mixed‑case referer hosts may fail to match even though comparison intends to be case‑insensitive.

Because this migration inserts embeddable_hosts rows with raw SQL, any existing embeddable_hosts values that include http:// or /https:// or path segments won’t go through the EmbeddableHost model’s normalization, so the new host lookup (which compares only the bare host) may fail for migrated data. Consider ensuring that migrated hosts are normalized to the same format as newly created EmbeddableHost records so existing embedding configurations keep working.

The contents of `category_fabricator.rb` and `embeddable_host_fabricator.rb` have been swapped, resulting in the loss of original category fabricators and potentially causing errors in fabricator usage.

The SQL query in the `app/controllers/admin/embeddable_hosts_controller.rb` file uses string interpolation (`'#{h}'`) to insert values, which is vulnerable to SQL injection. It should use parameter binding or proper quoting to prevent this security vulnerability.

The migration accesses execute(...)[0]['id'] without checking if the query returned any rows, which causes a crash when no embed_category setting exists. This can lead to a broken feature when attempting to edit category/host relationships.

discourse-graphite__4.text: The PollFeed job calls open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url) without validating the URL, allowing an attacker who controls the feed_polling_url site setting to make the server fetch arbitrary internal or external URLs.
The current origin validation using indexOf is insufficient and can be bypassed. An attacker could use a malicious domain like evil-discourseUrl.com to pass this check.
postMessage targetOrigin should be the origin (scheme+host+port), not the full referrer URL; using the full URL will cause the message to be dropped and prevent resizing.

The code sets X-Frame-Options: ALLOWALL which completely disables clickjacking protection. The referer validation can be bypassed (referer headers are easily spoofed), and the fallback to empty string for nil referer masks validation failures.

The TopicEmbed.import method is susceptible to a NoMethodError if the contents parameter is nil when attempting to append a string, and an XSS vulnerability due to unescaped url interpolation in the generated HTML.
The ERB block closes with end if, which is invalid Ruby/ERB and will raise at render; it should just be end to close the if block.

Calling `i.content.scrub` assumes that `i.content` is always populated. However, many RSS feeds do not provide a `content` field, leading to a potential nil pointer exception when `i.content` is nil. A fallback to `description` should be implemented to prevent crashes.

An unescaped request header (request.referer) is interpolated into JavaScript without proper escaping, which can lead to XSS vulnerabilities if the referer contains malicious content. This issue can allow attackers to execute arbitrary scripts in the context of the application.

discourse-graphite__6.text: The include_website_name method is missing the required ? suffix. Rails serializers expect include_ methods to end with ? for conditional attribute inclusion, a convention followed by other methods in this serializer. Without it, the website_name attribute may not be conditionally included as intended. Additionally, the '.' << website_host string concatenation should be replaced with '.' + website_host or '.#{website_host}' to avoid mutating string literals, which can lead to issues.

discourse-graphite__9.text: The @loaded_locales instance variable in translate_accelerator.rb is lazily initialized and accessed by multiple concurrent threads without synchronization.

Consider normalizing the input locale (e.g., to a symbol) when checking/loading here to avoid double-loading if the same locale is passed as a String vs Symbol (also applies to other locations in the PR).

keycloak__37038.text: In GroupPermissionsV2.canManage(), the permission fallback checks for both VIEW and MANAGE scopes (hasPermission(null, AdminPermissionsSchema.VIEW, AdminPermissionsSchema.MANAGE)), but canManage() should only grant access for MANAGE scope, not VIEW. This means users with only VIEW permission on groups can pass the canManage() check, granting them write access they should not have. The canView() method correctly checks both VIEW and MANAGE, but canManage() should only check MANAGE.

In getGroupIdsWithViewPermission, hasPermission is called with groupResource.getId() and the same groupResource.getId() is added to granted, but hasPermission resolves resources by name (treating the argument as a group id) and the GroupPermissionEvaluator contract says this method returns group IDs that are later used as UserModel.GROUPS and in getUsersCount group filters. This mismatch means per-group VIEW_MEMBERS/MANAGE_MEMBERS permissions may not yield the expected group IDs for filtering and counts, and evaluation may effectively only look at the type-level 'all-groups' resource; consider revisiting whether this should operate on the underlying group ids (resource names) instead so it aligns with the JPA queries and the interface contract.

keycloak__37429.text: The translation is in Italian instead of Lithuanian. This should be translated to Lithuanian to match the file's locale (messages_lt.properties).
The totpStep1 value uses Traditional Chinese terms in the Simplified Chinese file (zh_CN), which is likely incorrect for this locale. Please verify the locale‑appropriate translation.

The anchor sanitization logic has a potential issue where it consumes English matcher groups without proper validation. If the translated text has more anchor tags than the English text, this could lead to incorrect validation results.
Field HTML_TAGS should be declared as 'private static final' following Java naming conventions for constants
